'''George Ross Ihaka''' (born 1954)<ref>{{cite book |last=Wickham |first=Hadley |date=2014 |title=Advanced R |location=New York |publisher=Chapman and Hall/CRC |page=437 |isbn=9780429192678}})</ref> is a New Zealand [[statistician]] who was an associate professor of statistics at the [[University of Auckland]] until his retirement in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/en/about/news-and-events-5/news/news-2017/2017/12/ross-ihaka-retires.html|title=Ross Ihaka retires from the Department of Statistics – The University of Auckland|website=stat.auckland.ac.nz|access-date=2018-09-17}}</ref> Alongside [[Robert Gentleman (statistician)|Robert Gentleman]], he is one of the creators of the [[R (programming language)|R programming language]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ihaka|first1=R.|last2=Gentleman|first2=R.|year=1996|title=R: A Language for Data Analysis and Graphics|journal=Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics|volume=5|issue=3|pages=299–314|doi=10.2307/1390807|jstor=1390807}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Vance|first=Ashlee|author-link=Ashlee Vance|date=7 January 2009|title=Data Analysts Captivated by R's Power|url=//www.nytimes.com/2009/01/07/technology/business-computing/07program.html|website=The New York Times|access-date=2009-01-07}}</ref><ref name="nzh" /> In 2008, Ihaka received the [[Pickering Medal]], awarded by the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]], for his work on R.<ref>[http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/pickering-medal/recipients/ Pickering Medal: Recipients], Royal Society of New Zealand.</ref>

== Education==
Ihaka completed his undergraduate education at the [[University of Auckland]], and obtained his [[PhD]] in 1985 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] supervised by [[David R. Brillinger]].<ref name=mathgene/> His thesis was on statistical modelling for [[seismic interferometry]] and was titled [[Rūaumoko]], after the god of earthquakes, volcanoes and seasons in [[Māori mythology]].<ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy}}</ref><ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|url=https://search.library.berkeley.edu/permalink/01UCS_BER/1thfj9n/alma991057552089706532|publisher=University of California, Berkeley|website=berkeley.edu|year=1985|first=George Ross|last=Ihaka|oclc=910485430|title= Rūaumoko |id={{ProQuest|303363827}}|degree=PhD}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~brill/students.html| title=David R. Brillinger's students| access-date=14 August 2014| website=stat.berkeley.edu | publisher=Department of Statistics, University of California, Berkeley}}</ref>

==Career and research==
As of 2010, he was working on a new statistical programming language based on [[Lisp (programming language)|Lisp]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Compstat 2008|first1=Ross|last1=Ihaka|first2=Duncan|last2=Temple Lang|chapter=Back to the Future: Lisp as a Base for a Statistical Computing System |date=25 August 2008|pages=21–33 |doi=10.1007/978-3-7908-2084-3_2|isbn=978-3-7908-2083-6 |chapter-url=//www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/%7Eihaka/downloads/Compstat-2008.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite conference|title=R: Lessons Learned, Directions for the Future|first=Ross|last=Ihaka| url=//www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/%7Eihaka/downloads/JSM-2010.pdf|conference=Joint Statistical Meetings 2010, Statistical Computing Section|date=2010}}</ref> The Department of Statistics at the University of Auckland started a public lecture series in his honour in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stat.auckland.ac.nz/en/about/our-department/ihaka-lectures.html|title=Ihaka Lecture Series – The University of Auckland|website=stat.auckland.ac.nz|access-date=2018-09-17}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Ihaka is of [[Ngāti Kahungunu]], [[Rangitāne]] and [[European New Zealanders|Ngati Pākehā]] (New Zealand European) descent.<ref name="nzh">{{cite web |last1=Middleton |first1=Juliet |title=Academic unfazed by rock star status |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=10551243 |language=en-NZ |date=9 January 2009 |website=The New Zealand Herald}}</ref><ref name=off>{{Official URL}}</ref>
